### `EmbedResources`

```csharp
bool EmbedResources { get; set; }
```

Always carry resource bytes in the definition (`data`), even where `ResourceRef` would name them.

### `OnUnrepresentable`

```csharp
DefinitionUnrepresentable OnUnrepresentable { get; set; }
```

What to do with a construct a definition cannot express. The default is to fail, writing nothing.

### `ResourceRef`

```csharp
Func<DefinitionResourceDescriptor, string> ResourceRef { get; set; }
```

Names a resource the host can supply again when the definition is read. Return a name and the definition carries `ref` and a `sha256` instead of the bytes; return `null` to embed them. The writer never invents a name.

### `Target`

```csharp
string Target { get; set; }
```

The definition version to write, `"1.0"`. Anything this release cannot write is refused.

### `WritePaletteTokens`

```csharp
bool WritePaletteTokens { get; set; }
```

Write a palette token (`slate-800`) where a colour equals a palette entry exactly, instead of hex.
